mainEntity.name: What time is Ganga Aarti in Varanasi today?

acceptedAnswer.text: Evening Ganga Aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat: 5:30 PM (winter Oct-Mar), 7:00 PM (summer Apr-Jun). Morning Aarti at Assi Ghat: 5:30 AM (winter), 4:45 AM (summer). Arrive 45 minutes early for good viewing spots.

mainEntity.name: How long is the Ganga Aarti ceremony?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Ganga Aarti ceremony lasts 40-45 minutes. It includes conch blowing, synchronized lamp movements by 7-8 priests, incense offerings, and Sanskrit chants.

mainEntity.name: Is morning or evening Ganga Aarti better?

acceptedAnswer.text: Evening aarti at Dashashwamedh is more spectacular with grand fire rituals and crowds. Morning aarti at Assi Ghat is serene, intimate, with yoga and 20% fewer tourists. First-timers should see evening; spiritual seekers prefer morning.

mainEntity.name: Can I watch Ganga Aarti from a boat?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! Boat viewing costs ₹200-300 per person (shared) or ₹1,800-4,500 (private). Boats depart 45 minutes before aarti. Benefits: no crowds, eye-level flame views, better photos. Book via WhatsApp: +91 94503 01573.

mainEntity.name: Does Ganga Aarti happen every day?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Ganga Aarti happens 365 days a year at both Dashashwamedh and Assi Ghats. Even during monsoon storms or festivals, the ceremony is performed (may be moved indoors or shortened during extreme weather).

mainEntity.name: When is Dev Deepawali Ganga Aarti in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dev Deepawali 2026 falls on November 24 (Tuesday). The special aarti runs 5:15 PM - 7:50 PM (2.5 hours vs normal 45 min). 1 million+ diyas are lit across 84 ghats. Arrive by 3 PM; book boats 5-7 days in advance.
